ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The study of species' ecological niches has important significance for biodiversity conservation. Researchers investigated the distribution and diurnal activity rhythms of the white eared pheasant and the blood pheasant in three vegetation types in a nature reserve in our country; the results are shown in the table below. Do the differences in the distribution of the two species in the three vegetation types reflect the horizontal structure or the vertical structure of the community?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The study of species' ecological niches has important significance for biodiversity conservation. Researchers investigated the distribution and diurnal activity rhythms of the white eared pheasant and the blood pheasant in three vegetation types in a nature reserve in our country; the results are shown in the table below. Do the differences in the distribution of the two species in the three vegetation types reflect the horizontal structure or the vertical structure of the community?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a table of investigation results. The left side lists three vegetation types: mixed coniferous and broad-leaved forest, coniferous forest, and shrubland; the table headers respectively give the distribution proportion of the white eared pheasant (dry season, rainy season) and the distribution proportion of the blood pheasant (dry season, rainy season). The table shows that the distribution proportions of the two species in different vegetation types are different; below there are also diurnal activity rhythm curves of the two species. Reasoning: The question restricts the examination to “the differences in the distribution of the two species in the three vegetation types.” The horizontal structure of a community refers to differences in organism distribution among different sections, different habitats, or different vegetation types; the vertical structure refers to stratification within the same community at different height levels, such as the tree layer, shrub layer, and herb layer. Here what is compared is the distribution difference among three vegetation types, not the distribution at different height levels within the same vegetation, so what is reflected is the horizontal structure of the community.
